clue.text: For instance horse running round pound got much bigger

indicators.note: running round says the first piece encircles the second, wrapping around it

parts.note: a horse is an example of a four-legged animal, a quadruped
L is the abbreviation for a pound sterling (from Latin libra)

explanation.surface: A racehorse circling the paddock somehow grew enormously in size.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For instance horse' reads as a horse doing the running, but the phrase means the class a horse belongs to. 'running round' sets that word around L.
explanation.definitionFit: Something increased fourfold has grown greatly, so the past tense fits 'got much bigger'.

clue.text: Leave fairly shortly

indicators.note: shortly here asks for the word cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: fairly in the sense 'rather, somewhat' is a synonym of quite

explanation.surface: Depart rather soon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' looks like 'soon' but tells you to clip the last letter, E, from QUITE.
explanation.definitionFit: To quit a place or job is to depart from it, a direct verb synonym.

clue.text: Fodder area covered by an 'ole, conceivably

indicators.note: in a down entry, a piece covered by another sits beneath it, so it comes last

parts.note: a whole is two halves; with the H dropped Cockney-style, as in 'ole, that is 'alf 'alf

explanation.surface: Animal feed spread over a patch of ground with a hole in it, maybe.
explanation.walkthrough: The dropped H of 'ole signals Cockney speech, so the two halves making up a whole also lose their H: ALF ALF, with A for area placed underneath.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfalfa, also called lucerne, is a plant grown as livestock feed, so it is a kind of fodder.

clue.text: Create a commotion to make building taller

definitions.meaning: the idiom means to make a great deal of noise, cheering or complaining loudly
taken literally, lifting the top covering of a house adds height to it

explanation.surface: Kick up a fuss in order to add storeys to a house.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for making a huge noise is literally lifting the top covering of a building higher.

clue.text: See, coming up amid turmoil, underground explorer

indicators.note: amid places one piece in the middle of the other

parts.note: a pother is a commotion or fuss, a state of turmoil

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning 'see!' or 'behold'

explanation.surface: Someone spots a caver emerging from chaos below ground.
explanation.walkthrough: LO, reversed by 'coming up' to OL, goes 'amid' POTHER, an old word for fuss.
explanation.definitionFit: A potholer is a caver, someone who explores cave systems beneath the ground.

clue.text: A heart is lifted taking in one piece by Beethoven

indicators.note: taking in means the piece swallows another piece inside it
in a down entry, lifted means turned upward, read from bottom to top

parts.note: the core of something is its heart or centre
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A spirit raised by a single Beethoven composition.
explanation.walkthrough: CORE turned by 'is lifted' gives EROC, followed by A; 'taking in' then puts I inside: ERO-I-CA.
explanation.definitionFit: The Eroica is the popular name for Beethoven's Third Symphony, one of his best-known works.

clue.text: Nothing more than a lake

definitions.meaning: the adjective sense: only, simply, as in a trifling sum
a literary or regional word for a lake or pond, as in Windermere

explanation.surface: Just a body of water and nothing else.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means only or simply; the noun is a poetic word for a still pool or lake.

clue.text: One demands payment directly from member of the cast

parts.note: ex means straight from a place, as in goods priced ex works
a cast is made up of actors

explanation.surface: Someone collects money straight from one of the performers.
explanation.definitionFit: An exactor is a person who insists on or extorts payment, such as a tax gatherer.

clue.text: Fielder, wide perhaps, caught series of balls

parts.note: in cricket a wide is one kind of extra, a run not scored off the bat
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
in cricket an over is a set of six balls bowled from one end

explanation.surface: A cricket scene: a fielder stands wide, a catch is taken, an over is bowled.
explanation.walkthrough: Every piece is cricket: a wide is an extra, C is caught, and an over is six deliveries.
explanation.definitionFit: Extra cover is a fielding position on the off side in cricket, so the person stationed there is a fielder.

clue.text: Fashionable novels, when about fifty, can be an imposition

parts.note: in means trendy or fashionable

indicators.note: about means placed round, so the novels word surrounds the numeral

parts.note: novels are works of fiction
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Trendy novels, once their author turns fifty, become a burden to read.
explanation.definitionFit: Inflicting a penalty imposes it on someone, so the noun is a burden imposed.

clue.text: Inclination to use jargon

definitions.meaning: the special language of a group, such as thieves' slang

explanation.surface: A tendency to speak in technical terms.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a tilt or bevel; the other is insincere or specialised talk peculiar to a group.

clue.text: Cromwell's force making mark in terrible war with old enemy

indicators.note: in places the mark letter inside the rearranged letters
terrible suggests something wrecked or mangled, so these words are rearranged

parts.note: M stands for mark, the old German currency

explanation.surface: Cromwell's troops leave their mark in a dreadful conflict against an ancient foe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terrible' scrambles WAR, OLD and ENEMY into NEW-ODEL-ARMY; 'in' puts M among them.
explanation.definitionFit: The New Model Army was the Parliamentarian army formed in 1645 that Cromwell led in the English Civil War.

clue.text: Sportsman at university is dirty

definitions.meaning: at Oxford or Cambridge, someone who represents the university at a sport is awarded a ...
... means risqué or smutty, as in a ... joke

explanation.surface: A student athlete who is covered in mud.
explanation.definitionFit: An Oxbridge sporting representative is called after the colour award; the same colour word means indecent.

clue.text: Company playing to Archers fans

definitions.note: a body of musicians performing together

indicators.note: fans as a verb means spreads out, so these letters are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: A band performs for devotees of The Archers, a long-running BBC radio soap set in a farming village.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fans' looks like a noun for devotees, but as a verb it spreads TO ARCHERS out into a new order.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of musicians performing together forms a large ensemble, so a playing company fits.

clue.text: Precarious plight came without emotion

indicators.note: precarious means unstable, so these letters are unsettled into a new order

explanation.surface: A shaky situation arose and was met calmly.
explanation.definitionFit: A stolid, unexcitable temperament shows little feeling, the old humour theory's calm type.

clue.text: Husband gripped by pagan bird on moor

indicators.note: gripped by means held inside the following word

parts.note: a heathen is a pagan, one outside the main religions

explanation.surface: A married man is seized by a pagan on the moorland.
explanation.definitionFit: This extinct North American grouse lived on open scrubby heathland, so it is a moorland bird.

clue.text: One starting to develop sacked by Rome

indicators.note: sacked means plundered and wrecked, so the letters are ransacked into a new order

explanation.surface: A rising power is plundered by the Romans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sacked' looks like the Roman conquest of a city, but it signals the rearrangement of BY ROME.
explanation.definitionFit: An organism in its earliest stage of growth is just beginning to form, so the noun fits.

clue.text: Having a spell without web is attractive

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the spell word sits outside the web word

parts.note: magic is a spell or enchantment
a net is a mesh or web

explanation.surface: Someone charming even when offline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' reads as 'lacking the web', but here it has its old sense of outside: the spell surrounds the web.
explanation.definitionFit: Magnets draw things to them, so the adjective also means alluring or captivating.

clue.text: Rule of legislator in Irish Republic

indicators.note: in places the lawmaker inside the country's name

parts.note: Eire is the Irish-language name of Ireland
an MP, Member of Parliament, makes laws

explanation.surface: Government by a lawmaker sitting in Dublin.
explanation.definitionFit: Supreme dominion or sovereignty over territory is a sense of the noun, as in the empire of the seas.

clue.text: Grassland beyond river

parts.note: past means beyond, as in past the church
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire, a crossword regular

explanation.surface: Meadows stretching beyond the river bank.
explanation.definitionFit: Land covered with grass for grazing livestock is the standard meaning.

clue.text: Good-looking things added in house

indicators.note: in places the additions inside the dwelling word

parts.note: a home is a house
ands are additions, as in 'no ifs or ands'

explanation.surface: Attractive extras installed in a dwelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Handsome describes an attractive appearance, a straight synonym of comely.

clue.text: Old boy's place, filthy

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for an old boy, a former pupil; the 's links the two pieces
a scene is the place where something happens

explanation.surface: A former pupil's haunt is squalid.
explanation.definitionFit: Obscene means indecent or foul, so it matches filthy in its moral sense.

clue.text: Live on edge

parts.note: re means on or concerning, as in business letters
a side is an edge or border

explanation.surface: Dwell on the brink.
explanation.definitionFit: To dwell somewhere permanently is to live there, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Is cabinet minister engaged by Mr Cameron finally to rule badly?

indicators.note: engaged by means held within, so the first pieces sit inside MR

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
Michael Gove served in David Cameron's cabinet

indicators.note: finally picks only the last letter of the name

explanation.surface: Was a cabinet minister hired by David Cameron to govern poorly?
explanation.walkthrough: 'engaged by Mr' puts the first pieces between the two letters of Mr; 'finally' takes Cameron's last letter. Michael Gove was a minister in Cameron's British government.
explanation.definitionFit: The prefix mis- means wrongly, so to misgovern is to govern badly.

clue.text: Stay in Sunset Blvd maybe

parts.note: Sunset Boulevard is a thoroughfare in Los Angeles, LA
a boulevard is a kind of street, abbreviated ST

explanation.surface: Remain on the famous Hollywood boulevard.
explanation.walkthrough: Sunset Blvd is an example of an LA ST, a Los Angeles street.
explanation.definitionFit: To last is to endure or continue, the verb sense of stay as in 'it won't stay fine'.

clue.text: American pressman not new

parts.note: US is short for United States, so American
ED is the abbreviation for editor, a newspaper man

explanation.surface: An American journalist who is past his prime.
explanation.definitionFit: Second-hand goods have been previously owned, so they are no longer fresh from the shop.

clue.text: Time to embrace hooligan

parts.note: to hug is to embrace

explanation.surface: It's time to hug the yob.
explanation.definitionFit: A violent ruffian or rough is a near synonym of a hooligan.

clue.text: Resentment of female marsh bird apparently

definitions.meaning: a feeling of sourness or rancour at being treated badly
a bittern is a marsh bird, and -ess is a feminine ending as in lioness, so jokingly a hen bittern

explanation.surface: Anger felt by a hen wading bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Resentment is lingering sourness; adding a feminine suffix to the heron-like wading bird jokingly gives the same word.

clue.text: Team was exultant

definitions.meaning: a group of people working together, as on a ship
the past tense of crow, to boast triumphantly

explanation.surface: The side gloated over its win.
explanation.definitionFit: A working group aboard a vessel is the noun; the old past tense of the verb crow means boasted in triumph.

clue.text: Live with migraine possibly on high cliff

parts.note: to be is to exist or live
a migraine is one example of an aching head

explanation.surface: Coping with a headache while perched up on a tall clifftop.
explanation.walkthrough: Beachy Head is a chalk headland on the East Sussex coast in southern England, Britain's highest sea cliff.
explanation.definitionFit: This chalk headland in East Sussex is famous as the tallest sea cliff in Britain.
